purpose: Agent-readable contract for the R3.0-011 competency-question lifecycle: explicit Task selector, question/draft/review/freeze schemas, the public projection, visibility rules, and the v3 hidden-batch acceptance hand-off. It describes schema, phase, status and visibility only and carries no business answers. Review may be submitted by the business user or by an explicitly delegated Delivery Agent; the delegation is recorded with its authorization and source/version basis and never changes private visibility or independent Judge acceptance. It is only in force for a Team Task that declares parameters.competency_question_acceptance: true; tasks without the selector never load this contract and never get the competency-question capability.

task_parameter.name: competency_question_acceptance
task_parameter.rule: Explicit boolean Task-level selector. A run keeps the schema it started with; turning the parameter on inside an existing run to skip a stage is forbidden. Without the selector the R3.0-002 and existing R2.3 paths do not load any competency-question contract, role, bind, or capability.

lifecycle.rule: A rejection, modification, deletion, supplement, or stale revision returns only the affected panorama/slice stage to draft/review. The same competency-question session continues across phases; frozen means the current pool is delivered, not that the session has ended. A turn that ends while waiting for the user is not a task terminal state.

draft.transport: Runner-private capability cq_publish_question_draft only; drafts are never written into a shared directory by the agent.
draft.phase_rule: Only panorama-review and slice-review request formal review. Other lifecycle phases only save an immutable private draft and return preparation_saved with a republish instruction, without changing the current CQ phase, opening a Host review request or entering the reviewed pool. For panorama-draft/slice-draft, review_phase names the corresponding formal phase; otherwise the Agent must choose the appropriate review phase.

field_types.question: non-empty string
field_types.scope: object with exactly the keys kind and slice_ids; see scope below
field_types.evidence_refs: list of objects, each exactly {source, locator} with non-empty string values
field_types.unknown: list of strings; use [] when nothing is explicitly unknown; never a plain string, null, or object
field_types.content_version: integer >= 1 (JSON number; never a string, float, or boolean)

minimal_example.question: <one concrete business question about the approved material>

evidence_refs.source: <exact relative path under sources/ or exact interview_ref>

optional_runner_fields._exposed_to: Runner-owned list of roles that ever saw this question or answer; non-empty forces permanent public visibility at freeze time.

scope.slice_ids: non-empty for kind=slice, empty for kind=panorama

review.transport: Outer FIFO/stdin action cq_review only; never Team Transport and never routed through Coordinator.
review.delegated_delivery: When the host explicitly delegates review to Delivery, submit_cq_review.note records the delegation, authorization reference, source/material version, current question version, and point-by-point reasons. This is a user-authorized Agent decision, not a claim of per-question human approval; review binding, hidden/public visibility, freeze, and independent Consumer/Judge contracts remain unchanged.
review.binding: review_id, content_version and content_digest must match the published review snapshot; a mismatch rejects only this input.

public_projection.visibility: Approved public questions and answer points only. No hidden id, hidden text, answer hints, competency-question private conversation, or unreviewed record may appear.

freeze.immutability: Frozen pools and reference answers are never rewritten in place. A user revision produces a new question version with a new review binding and records the affected questions and slices; previous versions, answers and verdicts stay readable and unchanged.

visibility_rules.shown_implies_public: A question or answer shown to coordinator, modeling, protocol, or any other production role is permanently public and can never return to hidden.
visibility_rules.shared_evidence: Shared evidence may record IDs, digests, statuses and paths; it must never carry hidden question text, answer text, or competency-question private conversation.

scenario_map_rule: The existing r3-0-002 scenario-map cross_slice_competency_questions section keeps its three-field entry shape and may only reference questions present in the published public projection (matching question_id and question text), or be explicitly empty with the cross-slice coverage gap recorded. Production roles must not author new cross-slice question text from raw material. Consistency is checked Runner-side; the map entries carry no provenance fields.

question_count_guidance.rule: Counts are coverage suggestions for the user. They are never a Runner validity gate and never a run failure condition; the approved list drives the batch.

model_binding.timing: Bound at acceptance start, never at freeze time. The freeze snapshot is not bound to a model workspace.
checks: every explicit Ontology in the batch is authorized for this run
each authorized Ontology carries an observable model state digest
model state is re-verified after the batch; drift marks the batch incomplete instead of reusing a previous PASS

acceptance.rule: model-recall-insufficient requires modeling-quality; platform-runtime-incomplete requires runtime/infrastructure, platform-contract or collaboration/routing according to the first failure layer, including irrelevant or misbound read evidence. question-answer-review is a question state, not a fifth failure layer; a pure answer-review item may leave failure_layer empty and must not be counted as a model failure. Full PASS requires every question in the approved batch to carry a valid verdict with no pending review, no unexecuted item and no unsatisfied scope. An empty hidden set or a slice without a valid hidden question keeps an explicit acceptance coverage gap and can never produce a whole-batch or whole-scenario PASS. R4.0-013 option A: model-recall-insufficient means end-to-end semantic consumption is unsatisfied after successful relevant reads, including Consumer omissions or errors; it is not proof of model absence or knowledge coverage. Review every required point for approved support and question scope, preserving necessary implicit conditions; an unsupported or out-of-scope obligation is question-answer-review, not a silently removed frozen point. Record each unmet point or false assertion, source/content_digest/locator, Consumer content, actual question_id/response_digest/artifact_path/result location, diagnosis and limits in readable note. Correct sufficient returned content supports Consumer diagnosis; conflicting model content supports model error; absence requires evidence covering a bounded semantic scope. Empty/no_match, partial, pagination/projection omissions or conflicts alone leave the cause undetermined; relevant empty reads are not automatically routing failures or outages. Another question's relevant existing response in the same packet is diagnostic corroboration only, never answer evidence or a basis for pass. The packet contains no original request or evidence_recheck; do not infer request parameters or read stability from digests. Host qualification of cited responses, this question and all corroborating questions against existing recheck and drift records is required before delivering model-state attribution; an unqualified diagnosis retains its original note/verdict but has effective cause undetermined. Do not add diagnostic queries, fields, enums, automatic note parsing or diagnostic counts. Supported business unknowns may pass; unrelated global declarations are not mandatory, false assertions and conclusion-changing boundaries still matter. Historical reports remain unchanged, and exposed cases count only as regression.
acceptance.read_only: The cq-acceptance command and both v3 sessions are read-only for the platform: no StartLedger write, no fresh semantic start consumption, no production run start, continue, or repair.

recovery_rule: Each reason code rejects only the current operation and returns the object, phase and retry guidance. The run keeps running; platform or runtime exhaustion produces platform-runtime-incomplete with the matching failure layer instead of a permanent run failure.
